items.subject: Petition under Section 15 (1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 6 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related matters), Regulations, 2020 for the grant of Category - Ill inter-State trading licence under Section 14 of the Electricity Act, 2003. Probus Smart Things Private Limited
items.pdf_digest:
Hearing dated 6.10.2026
2. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that the
Petitioner has already complied with all the requirements specified in the Trading
Licence Regulations, including the issuance of notice in the Newspapers inviting
suggestions/objections on the present application. However, no suggestions/ objections
have been received so far. Accordingly, the learned counsel prayed to reserve the
matter for orders. After hearing the learned counsel for the Applicant, the matter was
reserved for orders.
Analysis and Decision
3. We have perused the documents available on record. Regulation 6 of the Trading
Licence Regulations provides for the procedure for the grant of a trading licence as
under:
“6. Procedure for grant of licence
(1) Any person desirous of undertaking inter-State trading in electricity shall make
an application to the Commission for grant of licence in the manner specified in
Form-I appended to these regulations and such application shall be
accompanied by-
(a) Such application fee as prescribed by the Central Government from
time to time and shall be paid as per the procedure specified in Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Payment of Fees) Regulations, 2012,
as amended from time to time or any statutory re-enactment thereof.
(b) Copies of the annual reports in case of the persons incorporated under
the Companies Act, 1956 or Companies Act, 2013 including audited
accounts along with the Directors' Report, Auditors' Report, the Schedules
and notes to accounts for one Year immediately preceding the Year in
which the application has been made and the audited special balance
sheet as on any date falling within 30 days immediately preceding the date
of filing the application.
(2) The Applicant shall post complete application along with annexures and
enclosures on its website so as to facilitate access to the application by any
person through internet and shall keep them on the website till the disposal of
the application.
Order in Petition No. 529/TD/2026 Page 2

(3) The Applicant shall within 7 days after making such application, publish a
notice of its application, in two daily newspapers in Form II, with the following
particulars, namely:
************
(4) The Applicant shall within 7 days from the date of publication of the notice as
aforesaid submit to the Commission on affidavit the details of the notice published
and shall also file the original complete page of the newspaper in which the notice
has been published.
(5) The Applicant shall allow a period of 30 days to the public to file objections or
suggestions to the notice of application published in the newspapers.
(6) The Applicant shall file its reply before the Commission within 30 days from
the last date of receipt of objections or suggestions from the public.
(7) The Commission after consideration of the objections or suggestions received
in response to the notice published by the Applicant and its reply may reject the
application or may propose to grant licence.
(8) When the Commission proposes to grant licence, it shall publish a notice of
its proposal in two daily newspapers, as the Commission may consider
appropriate, stating the name and address of the person to whom it proposes to
issue the licence and with such other details as the Commission considers
appropriate, to invite further objections or suggestions to its proposal.”
4. The Applicant has submitted the application, as per Form I, along with the
requisite fees.
5. The Applicant has uploaded the complete application along with annexures and
enclosures on its website in terms of Clause (3) of Regulation 6 of the Trading Licence
Regulations, 2020 and has further placed on record the relevant copies of the
newspapers in original in which notice of its application has been published. As per
Regulation 6 (3) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, the Applicant was required
to publish notices of its application within 7 days of filing, in two daily newspapers with
circulation in each of the five regions, in addition to publications from Delhi, including
one economic daily. The Applicant, vide affidavit dated 10.9.2026, has submitted that
notices under sub-section (2) of Section 15 of the Act read with Clause (4) of Regulation
6 of the Trading Licence Regulations have been published by the Applicant company
Order in Petition No. 529/TD/2026 Page 3

13. On consideration of the above facts, after a preliminary examination, we find that
the Applicant meets the requirements as specified in the Trading Licence Regulations
for the grant of a Category 'III' trading licence. In view thereof, the Commission proposes
to grant a Category 'III' trading licence to the Applicant. We direct that a notice under
Clause (a) of Sub-section (5) of Section 15 of the Act be issued inviting further
suggestions or objections to the proposal of the Commission.
14. The Petition shall be listed for a final hearing on 5.11.2026.
sd/- sd/- sd/-
(Ravinder Singh Dhillon) (Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V)

items.subject: Petition under Section 14 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Transmission License and other related matters) Regulations, 2024 for amendment of the existing RTM Transmission Licence to POWERGRID Khavda II-C Transmission Limited. POWERGRID Khavda II-C Transmission Limited
items.pdf_digest:
3. The Petitioner has submitted that the Commission vide Order dated 30.5.2025 in
Petition No. 439/MP/2024 has approved amalgamation/ merger as well as the consequent
assignment of the transmission licence(s) of the Petitioner Nos.1 to 12 and to Petitioner
No. 13, i.e., the Present Petitioner. The relevant extracts of the said Order are as under:
“26. The Petitioners have sought assignment/ transfer of licences granted to
Petitioner No. 1 to Petitioner No. 12 in favour of Petitioner No. 13 pursuant to and
as an effect of the Scheme in terms of sub-section 17(3) of the Act. Given that we
have already accorded our approval to the amalgamation/merger of the Petitioner
Nos. 1 to 12 with the Petitioner No.13 in terms of the Scheme of Arrangement under
Section 230-232 of the Companies Act, we also accord in-principle approval the
consequent assignment of the transmission licences granted to Petitioner Nos. 1 to
12 in favour of Petitioner No. 13. Needless to add, consequent to the assignment of
licences, all rights, assets, liabilities and obligations of these licensees in respect of
the transmission business shall vest in Petitioner No. 13 i.e. POWERGRID Khavda
II-C Transmission Limited. POWERGRID Khavda II-C Transmission Limited shall
also remain bound by the terms and conditions of licences granted to Petitioner Nos.
1 to 12.
27. However, as noted above, the Scheme of Arrangement under Section 230-232
of the Companies has been filed before the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) for
its sanction and approval under the relevant provisions of the Companies Act, read
with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs’ Notification No. GSR 582(E) dated 13.6.2017
and Notification No. G.S.R 463(E) dated 5.6.2015 and the approval of the MCA
thereof is currently pending. Accordingly, the approval of the amalgamation/merger
as well as the consequent assignment of the transmission licence(s) of the
Petitioner Nos.1 to 12 with Petitioner No.13, as accorded by us in the foregoing
paragraphs, shall be subject to the MCA’s sanction and approval of the Scheme.
Further, upon the receipt of the MCA’s sanction and approval of the Scheme, the
Petitioners shall also place on record a copy of such sanction and approval
in the file of the present case.”
4. The Petitioner has further submitted that subsequent to the said order, i.e., in Petition
No. 439/MP/2024, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (hereinafter referred to as “MCA”) vide
order dated 27.1.2026 has approved the merger scheme. Merger Approval Order has been
filed with the Registrar of Companies, NCT of Delhi- I on 1.3.2026. Therefore,
POWERGRID Koppal Gadag Transmission Limited has been merged into POWERGRID
Khavda II C Transmission Limited.
5. The Petitioner, vide compliance affidavit dated 2.3.2026, in compliance with the
directions issued in Petition No. 439/MP/2024, has placed on record a copy of the Ministry
of Corporate Affairs’ (MCA) order dated 27.1.2026, granting sanction and approval to the
Order in Petition No. 516/TL/2026 Page 4

present Petitioner, POWERGRID Khavda II-C Transmission Limited. Consequent to the
said merger, the Petitioner filed the present Petition to incorporate “Implementation of 2
nos. of 220 kV Bus Sectionalizers at 220 kV level of Gadag-ll 400/220kV PS”, in
accordance with the Transmission Licence Regulations.
18. The Petitioner has made the Application as per Form-I and paid a fee of Rs. One lakh
as prescribed by the Central Government. As directed by the Commission, the Petitioner
has served a copy of the Application on the beneficiaries of the transmission project.
19. The Petitioner has published the notices on the e-filing portal of the Commission and
on its website in Form-II in English and Vernacular language. The Petitioner has also
published the notice digitally in all editions of ‘Deccan Herald’ and ‘Vijayvani’ (in English
and Kannada, respectively) on 2.6.2026. In response, the general public has not raised
any objection to the notices.
20. The Petitioner has served a copy of the application on CTUIL as required under
Section 15(3) of the Act and read with Regulation 5 (9) of the 2024 Transmission Licence
Regulations. CTUIL, vide its letter dated 11.6.2026, has recommended the amendment of
the existing transmission licence to include the transmission project of the Petitioner. The
relevant portion of the said letter dated 11.6.2026 is extracted as under:
“This has reference to petition filed by M/s POWERGRID Khavda ll-C Transmission
Limited before Hon’ble CERC under Section 14, 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and
CERC (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of Transmission License and other
related matters) Regulations, 2024 for amendment of existing transmission licence to
M/s POWERGRID Khavda ll-C Transmission Limited for executing the ISTS scheme
“Implementation of 2 nos. of 220kV Bus Sectionalizers at 220kV level of Gadag-ll
400/220kV PS” under RTM. In this regard, the following is submitted:
1. Justification of the ISTS scheme:
i) Gadag-ll 400/220kV PS is presently under construction with implementation
schedule of 24 months (SCoD - Dec’25) under the scheme “Transmission Scheme for
integration of Renewable Energy Zone (Phase-ll) in Koppal-ll (Phase-A) and Gadag-ll
(Phase-A) in Karnataka and expected by Jun’26. The broad scope includes 2x500
MVA, 400/220kV ICTs, Gadag-ll - Koppal-ll 400kV (quad) D/c line and 04 nos. of 220kV
line bays. In addition to above, the pooling station is being augmented with 7x500 MVA,
400/220kV ICTs, Gadag-ll - Koppal-ll 400kV (quad) 2nd D/c line, 1 no. of 400kV line
bay and 05 nos. of 220 kV line bays under the scheme “System strengthening at
Order in Petition No. 516/TL/2026 Page 12

23. The Petition shall be listed for hearing on 10.11.2026.
